title: Rename the `type` input of `action:button` / `action:icon` (to `actionType`) so it stops colliding with the SDUI discriminator — objectstack#14490 ruling A, objectui half
body:
Filed by the director seat (objectstack #12708, summon #10, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`) to carry the objectui half of a maintainer ruling. Filed unassigned; `domain:ui`, `pm:queue`. objectstack#14490 is `pm:blocked` on this card.

## Ruling being implemented

Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-02, decision batch #13 item 4 on objectstack#14490, recommendation A, verbatim 「同意」.

Ruled: the collision between the component input named `type` on `action:button` and `action:icon` (the only two of 57 manifest components that declare one) and the SDUI envelope discriminator `type` is removed at the source. The input is renamed (working name `actionType`; the implementer may pick a better one if the objectui component config already has a convention) in the objectui component configuration; the pinned `sdui.manifest.json` in objectstack follows. No alias, no transition window (maintainer's standing 不渐进 rule); the changeset names the rename.

## Why

- On the html tier the discriminator refusal landed by objectstack PR #14274 makes `type=` unauthorable, and its prescription ("write the tag you meant") is wrong for these two components.
- On the react tier the same collision is rescued by `specType` (objectui#2880); the 2026-09-01 ruling declined to bring that alias to the html tier.
- A declared input that one tier cannot author is a permanent special case in every doc, refusal message and future source format. Renaming removes the special case for every tier at once.

## First step (measure, then rename)

Census the real usage of `action:button.type` and `action:icon.type` in this repo (component config, examples, schema catalog, console, docs) and in the shipped example apps. objectstack's own census covered only html-tier sources in that repo and found zero; the react-tier population lives here and is unmeasured. Whatever the count, the rename lands directly with the census in the PR body; the count decides the changeset wording, not the direction.

## Scope

- objectui: the component config declaring the input; every read site of the prop in the two action renderers; `specType` rescue left as-is (it addresses other collisions); docs pages that show the prop; catalog entries.
- objectstack (follow-up, not this card): `sdui.manifest.json` pin bump; the html-tier refusal then needs no component-aware special case; `content/docs/ui/react-pages.mdx` sentence not needed.

## Acceptance

- The manifest scan in objectstack#14490's re-check returns an empty list for inputs named `type` (control: the `variant` scan stays non-empty).
- An html-tier page setting the renamed input on `action:button` parses and renders.
- Clause-② yes (published component input renamed): `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; `@object-ui/*` changeset minor.

Related: objectstack#14490 (the finding and ruling), objectstack PR #14274 (the refusal), objectui#2880 (`specType`), objectstack #12708 (director seat ledger).
